subject.title: Feature Request: cron.defaults.delivery config for default delivery target

question: Should OpenClaw add a new global `cron.defaults.delivery` recipient default for scheduled output, and if so what safe precedence and validation policy should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding a default scheduled-output recipient is new config surface with privacy-sensitive routing behavior, so automation should not choose the product/security policy alone.

options.title: Design `cron.defaults.delivery`
options.body: Add the requested default with strict schema, explicit per-job precedence, recipient/account/thread validation, CLI/UI visibility, docs, and regression tests.

options.title: Keep explicit per-job delivery only
options.body: Reject the global default and document safer explicit `--channel`/`--to` workflows plus current fail-closed behavior.

options.title: Fold into broader output routing
options.body: Make this a subdecision of the broader cron output-target contract tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/49078 before implementing any default recipient field.

recommendation.title: Design `cron.defaults.delivery`
recommendation.body: Add the requested default with strict schema, explicit per-job precedence, recipient/account/thread validation, CLI/UI visibility, docs, and regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on the cron default boundary and prior triage context, while CODEOWNERS can handle the security review once direction is chosen.
